findings.title: Serialize index builds for the same key
findings.body: Restricting cacheMu to the final assignment allows multiple builds for the same namespace/resource to run concurrently. For an index skipped at startup, a search can begin building it while a watch event sees the cache miss and starts another build. The second index can receive subsequent watch updates before the slower first build replaces it in the cache with an older snapshot, losing updates or resurrecting deleted search results. Keep per-key build synchronization while allowing different keys to build concurrently.

findings.title: Synchronize TotalDocs with cache writes
findings.body: The event-handling goroutine starts before this new TotalDocs call. An event for an uncached namespace/resource can therefore invoke BuildIndex and modify bleveBackend.cache while TotalDocs iterates that map without acquiring cacheMu. This can terminate the process with a concurrent map iteration/write error during startup, even though the initial build errgroup has finished. TotalDocs needs to acquire the cache read lock or iterate a snapshot taken under that lock.

findings.title: Make watch consumers handle channel closure before eager initialization
findings.body: Eager initialization makes constructing and stopping an otherwise unused search-enabled SQL server start and then stop its watch pollers. When the SQL backend's Stop cancels the poller, the poller closes its event channel. searchSupport.init receives with `v := <-events` without checking whether the channel is closed, then passes nil to handleEvent, which dereferences evt.Type and panics. The server watch consumer has the same unchecked receive. Previously an unused server had not started these loops. Make both consumers exit on channel closure so the new construct-then-stop path does not crash the process.

findings.title: Retain stopped-state checks in request handlers
findings.body: Removing the per-request Init calls also removes the handlers' stopping/stopped checks: server.Stop sets initErr to those errors, which Init previously returned to callers. Create, Update, and Delete now reach the backend even after Stop. The SQL backend's Stop only cancels polling and leaves the database open, so these requests can commit successfully after watch/index propagation has ended. Preserve a separate running-state guard even though initialization is now eager.
